subjects.label: Match engine
subjects.description: How the simulated football plays out: defenders' positioning, shots hitting the bar or skied, weak-foot finishing, the AI's tactics and the pattern of results in the table; not the menus around the match or the wider career game.

subjects.label: Scripted results
subjects.description: The belief that the game decides matches rather than the players on the pitch: the AI cheating in big games, fouls and bounces conjured to hand one side chances, results that feel fixed; not ordinary complaints that the game is hard.

subjects.label: The new interface
subjects.description: The redesigned interface itself: the new layout against the old menus, pages nested inside pages, a confusing or headache-inducing screen, wasted space on wide displays and operations that feel backwards; not bugs that stop a screen working.

subjects.label: Missing and removed features
subjects.description: Features earlier editions had or players expected and cannot find: the timeline and end-of-season review, saved database search filters, managing a national team and details felt to be absent; not features that exist but work badly.

subjects.label: The two-year wait
subjects.description: The two years between this edition and the last, and whether what shipped justifies the gap; belongs only when the review weighs the game against the wait, not when it discusses patches after release.

subjects.label: Released unfinished
subjects.description: The claim that the game was sold before it was finished: it should not have been released or charged for in this state, buy it once the fixes land, or skip this edition and wait for the next; not individual bugs listed on their own.

subjects.label: Earlier editions and the series' direction
subjects.description: How this edition compares with the ones before it and where the series is heading: a console game aimed at a new audience, a bold new chapter, a franchise that has lost its core, not as good as the others; not comparisons with games from other series.

subjects.label: The backlash
subjects.description: The wave of negative reviews as a subject in itself: telling readers to ignore the complainers, saying the problems are exaggerated, or liking it although most people did not; not the reviewer's own complaint about the game.

subjects.label: Save stories
subjects.description: What happened in the reviewer's own career: the club taken to five straight titles, the champions they crowned, the newgens who took over world football, the side relegated every time; not the systems that produced those outcomes.
